title: News feed (Instagram / X style) client
summary: An infinite, media-heavy feed that opens instantly from cache, scrolls at 120fps, works offline for already-seen content, and supports likes and comments with optimistic updates.
requirements: Functional: scroll ranked feed, pull to refresh, like/comment, posts with images and video, new-posts indicator.
Non-functional: first content under 1s (from cache), no scroll hitches, bounded memory and data usage, offline read of cached feed.
Scale: 100M DAU, ~200 feed items viewed per session.
components: Feed API (BFF): `GET /feed?cursor=` returning items with author, media variants, counts, and `nextCursor`
FeedRepository: cache-first, merges network pages into local store
Local store (SQLite) for posts and authors (normalized), with TTL and size cap
Image pipeline: memory + disk cache, downsampling, prefetching, CDN URLs per size
Video player pool: reuse AVPlayer instances, autoplay only the most visible cell, muted by default
Impression tracker (visible > 50% for > 1s) batched to analytics
tradeoffs: Server-ranked feed keeps clients simple and consistent; client re-ranking allows instant personalization but duplicates logic.
Normalized storage (posts + users) keeps updates consistent (rename once) but costs joins; denormalized per-feed blobs are faster to render.
Aggressive prefetch improves smoothness but wastes data on cellular; adapt by network type and Low Data Mode.
Showing new posts automatically shifts content under the user; a 'new posts' pill is usually better UX.
body: **Launch path:** render the cached first page synchronously from SQLite, then refresh in the background and merge (diffable snapshot, keep scroll position).

**Media:** server returns multiple renditions (thumb, 1x, 2x, video HLS); client picks by cell size and network. Use blurhash/dominant color placeholders to avoid layout jumps; fixed aspect ratio from metadata.
**Optimistic like:** update local count and state immediately, enqueue mutation with idempotency key; on failure revert and show a toast. Server is the source of truth on next refresh.
**Memory:** cap decoded image cache by cost; release offscreen video players; window very long lists.
**Failure modes:** partial page decode errors (drop the item, not the page), stale cache after account switch (key by user), duplicate posts across pages (dedupe by ID).
**Metrics:** time to first post, scroll hitch rate, image load p95, feed refresh success rate, impressions per session.

code.caption: Post model (client)
code.text:
struct Post: Identifiable, Codable, Sendable {
    let id: String
    let authorID: String
    let createdAt: Date
    let text: String?
    let media: [Media]           // each with renditions + aspect ratio + placeholder
    var likeCount: Int
    var viewerHasLiked: Bool
}
